frozen_object.clock: physical diffusion time t>0; tau=log t only for the explicitly declared rescaled flow
frozen_object.equation: u_t=(u^m)_xx on R with m>0 and mass M>0
frozen_object.normalization: mass integral equals M; translations are excluded by centered normalization
frozen_object.profile_class: centered nonnegative integrable first-kind profiles of mass M with F^m locally absolutely continuous and (F^m)'+alpha*xi*F=0 almost everywhere; uniqueness is up to almost-everywhere equality

headline: All one-dimensional positive exponents admit a single mass-normalized Barenblatt similarity atlas with exact compact, Gaussian, algebraic-tail, moment, pressure, and rescaled-dissipation boundaries
nonclaims: priority for the porous-medium equation, Barenblatt profiles, fast diffusion, or Wasserstein gradient flow
classification of arbitrary Cauchy solutions, signed profiles, non-centered profiles, or higher dimensions
that finite rational-exponent regression proves the all-m theorem
free-energy dissipation without regularity, integrability, and boundary-decay hypotheses

route_a.strongest_failure: The flow is dissipative and supplies no rational-prime primitive owner, periodic ledger, target determinant, or same-clock unitary lift.
route_a.strongest_positive: The nonlinear diffusion has a source-native mass-preserving similarity flow and exact gradient-flow dissipation in its stated finite-energy class.

theorem.dissipation: for sufficiently regular positive rescaled solutions with finite displayed free energy (no infinity-minus-infinity) and justified boundary decay, dF_m/dtau=-integral v |partial_xi chemical_potential|^2; this is not asserted outside that class, and the unrenormalized Barenblatt free-energy/second-moment boundary is m>1/3 in fast diffusion
theorem.fast: for 0<m<1, F=(C+b_m xi^2)^(-1/(1-m)), b_m=(1-m)/(2m(m+1)), with algebraic tail
theorem.mass: C is uniquely fixed by the exact Beta integrals recorded in the theorem package
theorem.moments: all porous and Gaussian absolute moments are finite; in fast diffusion the r-th absolute moment is finite exactly when r<(1+m)/(1-m), logarithmically divergent at equality
theorem.porous: for m>1, F=(C-k_m xi^2)_+^(1/(m-1)), k_m=(m-1)/(2m(m+1)), with compact support
theorem.pressure: for m>1, P=m u^(m-1)/(m-1) is parabolic on support, X_+/-=+/-R_M t^alpha, and each one-sided interface satisfies X_+/-'=alpha X_+/-/t=-lim_inside P_x
theorem.rescaled: v_tau=(v^m)_(xi xi)+alpha(xi v)_xi and each mass-M Barenblatt profile is stationary
theorem.second_moment: the fast-diffusion second moment is finite exactly for m>1/3; m=1/3 is logarithmically divergent
theorem.uniqueness: uniqueness is only among centered nonnegative integrable zero-flux first-kind similarity profiles of mass M with F^m locally absolutely continuous and the integrated profile law holding almost everywhere, up to almost-everywhere equality; it is not uniqueness among arbitrary Cauchy solutions
